transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Sasha Nguyen (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (AstraMed Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Infra Lead), Hana Li (CTO), Daniel Reed (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be partial):
AstraMed is evaluating Redwood Dedicated reserved GPU pools for production inference of a clinical NLP/triage model. Primary concerns: strict data isolation, predictable throughput for peak days, burst capacity for spikes, integration with KMS and VPC peering, and cost vs latency tradeoffs. They asked about autoscaling, warm KV cache strategies, fallbacks to hosted instances, and SLAs for latency and uptime. Next steps: share pricing + burst policy, run a 24-hour benchmark with their prompt set, and deliver security artifacts.

Topics: Dedicated sizing, burst strategy, isolation and VPC, KMS/encryption, SLA/uptime, benchmarking plan, migration path

Action items (auto-block, some duplicated in metadata): see action_items field

Transcript:
[00:00] Elena Park: all right thanks everyone for joining, uh let's do quick intros and then we'll jump into the dedicated sizing questions. I'm Elena from Redwood, AE. Marco is our SE, Sasha on the config side.
[00:18] Priya Menon: Hi, Priya here, head of ML at AstraMed. We run a clinical triage model, mostly text classification and long-form summarization of patient notes.
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: Liam, infra lead, I deal with networking and on-prem connectors.
[00:32] Hana Li: Hana, CTO, I'll be here for architecture and procurement path.
[00:36] Daniel Reed: Daniel, security, quick questions on KMS and SOC2.
[00:40] Marco Diaz: cool, thanks. quick agenda — figure out your throughput needs, talk burst options, isolation/VPC and KMS, then next steps for benchmarks.

[02:05] Priya Menon: To start, our production traffic today is about 2k inference requests/day but it's spiky — certain clinics batch uploads and we see peaks to ~7–8k in a 3‑hour window. Avg token length is 350, but our summarization paths hit 1,200 tokens sometimes. Latency SLO is pretty tight: <500ms p50 for the short paths, p95 under 1.5s ideally. We do care about cost but reliability and isolation are top.

[04:10] Marco Diaz: thanks, that helps. with Dedicated you can reserve an entire GPU pool so performance is predictable. question: do you want a single tenant pool per environment (prod/staging) or a pooled reserved cluster with strict tenant mapping?

[04:40] Hana Li: For compliance we prefer single-tenant hardware for prod. Staging can be shared. Also we need to ensure no cross-tenant KV cache leakage.

[05:12] Sasha Nguyen: right, we do dedicated physical GPU pools for Dedicated customers. KV cache is per-customer isolated. there are a couple of caveats around warm cache after redeploys — warmup windows can be tuned and we can provide snapshot/restore of cache before a rollout.

[06:00] Liam O'Connor: how do you handle bursts? i.e., we might have 3x baseline for a few hours. can the dedicated pool autoscale? or do you recommend overprovisioning + burst credits?

[06:30] Marco Diaz: good question. two options: reserved baseline capacity + a burst lane onto a shared capacity that we reserve as needed, or reserve larger pool and rely on elastic GPU add-ons (contract dependent). Burst onto hosted shared can be automatic with policy-based routing, but that mixes isolation — we can do encrypted in transit and strict data controls, but it means the burst path is not single-tenant hardware.

[07:20] Priya Menon: We can't send PHI outside a single-tenant boundary. So bursting to shared hosted is risky for us. Is there a way to have reserved burst capacity that's still isolated?

[07:40] Elena Park: yes — for enterprise Dedicated contracts we offer the option to reserve a separate burst pool that's still dedicated to the customer but billed separately. it's basically a cold-standby capacity you can spin up for peaks. There is an extra monthly commitment but it keeps you in the single-tenant boundary.

[08:05] Daniel Reed: What about encryption and key management? KMS integration? HSM?

[08:25] Sasha Nguyen: we integrate with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, on-prem HSM via standard PKCS#11 patterns). Keys for token encryption and at-rest are customer-managed in the Private control plane for Dedicated as an enterprise add-on. We can provide key rotation and prove key access never leaves the customer's control plane.

[09:30] Hana Li: do you support VPC peering or private link so traffic never crosses public internet?

[09:42] Marco Diaz: yes, VPC peering and private egress are supported. we also have a private control plane option in Dedicated for customers that want their control plane in a VPC.

[10:05] Priya Menon: curious on expected throughput per GPU — our model is a 30B parameter transformer, quantized to int8 in some experiments. If we take quantized model, what's a ballpark of tokens/sec?

[10:28] Marco Diaz: ballpark depends on GPU flavor and sequence length. for a 30B at int8 on A100 equivalent with our optimizations you might see ~20–30 tokens/sec single-stream for long sequences; batching increases token throughput significantly. if you're batching real-time requests you'll see better throughput but latency tradeoffs. we'll put concrete numbers in the sizing doc.

[11:20] Liam O'Connor: sequence length variance is big here — some requests 300 tokens, others 1200. how does your scheduler handle that?

[11:35] Sasha Nguyen: scheduler is workload-aware; it will group by similar sequence length to avoid wasteful padding. we also support continuous batching with latency SLO constraints, and prefix caching for repeated context.

[12:10] Priya Menon: about prefix/KV caching — we do a lot of repeated prompts with same patient context during a shift. can cache be warmed across restarts? you mentioned snapshots, but what's the cost in memory?

[12:34] Marco Diaz: snapshots store the KV cache references; restore time depends on size. memory cost is proportional to sequence history per user; we can size cache nodes separately. for heavy caching workloads, we recommend a dedicated cache tier in the cluster — modest extra nodes but big latency gains on p50.

[13:40] Hana Li: curious about SLA — uptime and latency commitments for Dedicated?

[13:52] Elena Park: Dedicated comes with an SLA for availability (99.9% typical for reserved pools, configurable higher for enterprise). Latency SLOs are tied to instance sizing and config; we provide p50/p95 baselines in the onboarding benchmarks and commit to alerting and remediation runbooks. We'll share standard SLA doc.

[14:50] Priya Menon: can you explain the rollback/fallback path if a large rollout causes cache thrashing or regressions? we need safe canary behavior.

[15:10] Marco Diaz: we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model version if regeneration error rates exceed thresholds. KV cache warmup on rollback is supported via snapshots; we can also throttle traffic to the canary.

[16:05] Priya Menon: what about observability — token-level cost, per-route latency, traces?

[16:20] Sasha Nguyen: Console exposes token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, traces for request paths, and model-level metrics. you can export logs to SIEM and hook into DataDog or Splunk. all logs can be encrypted and we support retention controls.

[17:05] Daniel Reed: on compliance — SOC2, ISO, audit logs for key operations?

[17:18] Elena Park: we are SOC2 compliant, and for Dedicated enterprise we provide additional audit logs and evidence packages. we'll attach the security pack in the follow-up.

[18:10] Hana Li: procurement question: how are commitments structured? monthly vs annual, and how do we scale down if usage is lower?

[18:28] Elena Park: Reserved capacity is contractual — monthly or annual commits. we offer some flexibility for right-sizing at renewal windows; during the term scaling down typically needs negotiation. For short term spikes we recommend a separate burst pool rather than resizing the baseline.

[19:05] Liam O'Connor: another operational question — what about firmware/driver updates on the GPUs? we need maintenance windows and change control.

[19:22] Marco Diaz: maintenance windows are scheduled with the customer for Dedicated pools; we prioritize non-disruptive upgrades and provide advance notices and rollback plans.

[20:00] Priya Menon: for benchmarking — what's the minimal benchmark you need to estimate sizing?

[20:12] Marco Diaz: a representative prompt set with token distribution, a sample of peak concurrency (requests/sec) and target SLOs. ideally a 24-hour trace file and a few long sequences to test worst-case. we'll run both perf and stability tests and provide throughput/latency curves.

[21:00] Priya Menon: we can provide a day's production log anonymized and a few synthetic long prompts.

[21:20] Elena Park: perfect. we'll schedule a benchmark with Marco and Sasha to run in our staging Dedicated mirror. Priya, can you share those artifacts by Friday?

[21:33] Priya Menon: yes, I'll share by 2025-02-14.

[22:10] Hana Li: cost question — can you ballpark monthly cost for a reserved 4-GPU pool with an A100-equivalent for baseline and one smaller reserved burst node? rough numbers suffice.

[22:30] Elena Park: i can give a rough range now but we'll send detailed pricing. very rough: baseline 4x A100-eq reserved might be in the low 10s of thousands USD/month depending on region and support level; dedicated burst node reserve extra mid-thousands. exact depends on contract term and cloud footprint.

[23:05] Daniel Reed: do you offer encryption at rest by default and can we bring our own keys?

[23:18] Sasha Nguyen: yes, encryption at rest is standard, and BYOK via customer KMS is available. we'll include integration steps in the runbook.

[24:00] Priya Menon: one more — model quantization: will Redwood handle full int8 pipeline and what are expected quality regressions?

[24:18] Marco Diaz: we support multiple quantization profiles. quality impact depends on the model; we recommend an eval suite. our Optimize tooling can recommend profiles and run reg checks against your eval set. small regressions sometimes occur but often acceptable; we'll show tradeoffs in the benchmark report.

[25:05] Hana Li: let's talk timeline — we want production by Q3 2025, pilot in Q2. is that realistic?

[25:20] Elena Park: yes, Q2 pilot (benchmarks and 2–4 week pilot) and Q3 production is feasible. path depends on security review and procurement.

[26:00] Priya Menon: ok any blockers on our side? security will need SOC2 docs, Liam needs VPC peering instructions, and Priya will need a test tenant for benchmark.

[26:20] Liam O'Connor: also need clarity on network egress IPs and firewall rules.

[26:35] Sasha Nguyen: noted — we'll provide a network appendix with IP ranges and peering steps.

[27:10] Daniel Reed: about data retention — can we set short retention for logs and request payloads?

[27:25] Elena Park: yes retention is configurable at the org or route level; we can set minimal retention for sensitive workloads.

[28:00] Priya Menon: curious: if we do Dedicated but want to migrate to Private (on-prem) later, how disruptive is that?

[28:15] Marco Diaz: migration path is supported — models and configs are portable. the biggest lift is networking and on-prem hardware procurement. we can run a hybrid model during transition.

[29:00] Hana Li: procurement-wise, any standard redwood contract templates we can review?

[29:12] Elena Park: yes we will share redlined contract templates for Dedicated and the enterprise add-ons.

[30:00] Priya Menon: what about multi-region failover? we need DR for certain clinics.

[30:15] Marco Diaz: we support active-active and active-passive routing. for Dedicated we can provision cold-standby in another region and manage replication of KV cache snapshots. multi-region adds cost but meets DR needs.

[31:10] Liam O'Connor: any specific firewall/NAT requirements for VPC peering?

[31:25] Sasha Nguyen: standard inbound/outbound ranges, TLS mutual auth on control plane endpoints; we'll send the detailed network appendix.

[32:00] Hana Li: ok let's recap and next steps.

[32:12] Elena Park: recap — Redwood will: 1) send Dedicated pricing + SLA + burst policy, 2) schedule 24-hour benchmark once Priya shares traces, 3) provide SOC2/security pack and network appendix, 4) provide sizing doc for GPU flavors and expected throughput.

[33:10] Priya Menon: i will share the artifacts and liaise internally on procurement dates.

[34:00] Daniel Reed: please make sure encryption and KMS details are explicit in the docs.

[34:12] Sasha Nguyen: will do.

[35:00] Elena Park: any other questions?
[35:10] Priya Menon: none from me, thanks.
[35:14] Hana Li: no, good session.

[35:30] Marco Diaz: quick note — i'll include a few perf curves from similar 30B deployments in stale literature to set expectations.

[36:00] Elena Park: perfect, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule. thanks all.

[36:20] Meeting ended.
